dev-caches.npm.name: npm's download cache
dev-caches.npm.what: Copies of every package npm has downloaded, kept so that installing the same version again needs no download.
dev-caches.npm.made-by: npm, the package manager that comes with Node.js.
dev-caches.npm.if-removed: It goes to the Trash; the space comes back when you empty it. Your projects and the packages installed in them keep working.
dev-caches.npm.comes-back: Yes. npm downloads each package again the next time a project installs it, which needs the network and takes longer.
dev-caches.yarn.name: Yarn's download cache
dev-caches.yarn.what: Copies of the packages Yarn has downloaded, kept so that the next install needs no download.
dev-caches.yarn.made-by: Yarn, a package manager for JavaScript projects.
dev-caches.yarn.if-removed: It goes to the Trash; the space comes back when you empty it. Your projects and the packages installed in them keep working.
dev-caches.yarn.comes-back: Yes. Yarn downloads each package again on the next install that needs it, which needs the network and takes longer.
dev-caches.homebrew.name: Homebrew's downloads
dev-caches.homebrew.what: The packages and apps Homebrew downloaded to install or upgrade them. Once installed, they are not needed.
dev-caches.homebrew.made-by: Homebrew, the package manager for the command line.
dev-caches.homebrew.if-removed: They go to the Trash. Everything Homebrew installed keeps working; Homebrew tidies its own links to them on its next cleanup.
dev-caches.homebrew.comes-back: Only when Homebrew installs or upgrades something: it downloads what it needs then. Homebrew also clears old downloads on its own.
dev-caches.cargo.name: Cargo's downloaded crates
dev-caches.cargo.what: The crates (Rust libraries) Cargo downloaded from its registry, packed and unpacked, kept so that the next build needs no download.
dev-caches.cargo.made-by: Cargo, Rust's build tool and package manager.
dev-caches.cargo.if-removed: They go to the Trash. Your projects, Cargo's settings and the programs you installed with Cargo stay.
dev-caches.cargo.comes-back: Yes. Cargo downloads each crate again the next time a project builds with it, which needs the network.
dev-caches.cocoapods.name: CocoaPods' download cache
dev-caches.cocoapods.what: Copies of the libraries CocoaPods downloaded for iOS and macOS projects.
dev-caches.cocoapods.made-by: CocoaPods, a dependency manager for Swift and Objective-C projects.
dev-caches.cocoapods.if-removed: It goes to the Trash. Your projects keep the libraries already installed in them.
dev-caches.cocoapods.comes-back: Yes. CocoaPods downloads each library again the next time a project installs it.
dev-caches.gradle.name: Gradle's caches
dev-caches.gradle.what: Libraries Gradle downloaded and files it prepared for builds of Java, Kotlin and Android projects.
dev-caches.gradle.made-by: Gradle, the build tool of Java, Kotlin and Android projects, and the IDEs that run it.
dev-caches.gradle.if-removed: They go to the Trash. Your projects and Gradle's settings stay.
dev-caches.gradle.comes-back: Yes. The next build downloads and prepares them again, so it takes longer and needs the network.
dev-caches.pip.name: pip's download cache
dev-caches.pip.what: Copies of the Python packages pip downloaded or built, kept so that the next install is faster.
dev-caches.pip.made-by: pip, the package installer of Python.
dev-caches.pip.if-removed: It goes to the Trash; the space comes back when you empty it. Your projects and the packages installed in them keep working.
dev-caches.pip.comes-back: Yes. pip downloads each package again the next time it installs it.
dev-caches.go-build.name: Go's build cache
dev-caches.go-build.what: Compiled pieces of Go programs, kept so that the next build only compiles what changed.
dev-caches.go-build.made-by: The Go tools, on every build or test.
dev-caches.go-build.if-removed: It goes to the Trash. Your code and the programs you built stay.
dev-caches.go-build.comes-back: Yes. The next build compiles everything again, with no download; it is slower once.
dev-caches.xcode-derived-data.name: Xcode build data
dev-caches.xcode-derived-data.what: What Xcode makes while it builds and indexes a project: compiled files, the code index and build logs, one folder per project.
dev-caches.xcode-derived-data.made-by: Xcode, Apple's app for building apps.
dev-caches.xcode-derived-data.if-removed: It goes to the Trash. Your projects and their code stay; Xcode builds and indexes them again when you open them.
dev-caches.xcode-derived-data.comes-back: Yes. Xcode makes it again on the next build of the project, with no download; that build is slower.
dev-caches.enabled.label: Developer caches
dev-caches.enabled.description: Finds the download caches of package managers and Xcode's build data. The tools make them again when they need them.
dev-caches.finding.reason-download: {tool} downloads it again when it needs it.
dev-caches.finding.reason-build: {tool} builds it again when it needs it.
dev-caches.left-out.not-yours: Some of it belongs to the system or another user, or is locked, often after a command run with sudo. Removing it needs an administrator.
dev-caches.left-out.special: It holds a connection a running program may be using, so it is kept.
dev-caches.left-out.app-open: Its app is open and writes here as it works. Quit the app and scan again.
dev-caches.left-out.no-system: Fresher could not list your open apps, so it keeps this. Scan again.
